Saudi Machinery Firm Al-Mutlaq Engineering Enters Administration Amid Sector Challenges

Riyadh – Al-Mutlaq Engineering Co., a prominent Saudi Arabian manufacturer of industrial machinery, has entered administration following months of financial difficulty, the company announced on Sunday. The move marks one of the most significant insolvencies in the Kingdom’s machinery sector in recent years and has already led to a partial halt in the firm’s operations.

In a statement released late Sunday evening, the board of Al-Mutlaq Engineering confirmed the appointment of administrators from a local restructuring firm to oversee the company’s affairs. The statement cited “persistent cash flow pressures and a challenging market environment” as key factors behind the decision.

Founded in 1998 and headquartered in Riyadh, Al-Mutlaq Engineering has supplied assembly-line equipment, industrial presses, and automated systems for clients across Saudi Arabia and the Gulf region. The company employs more than 250 workers at its primary manufacturing plant in Riyadh’s industrial zone, with a smaller workforce at branches in Dammam and Jeddah.

At the factory gates on Monday morning, employees expressed concern about the future of their jobs. “We were told there will be a review of all departments and some temporary suspensions of production lines,” said a technician who requested anonymity. “Everyone is waiting for more information.”

The Saudi Machinery Manufacturers Association (SMMA) described the development as a “serious setback for the domestic industry.” “Al-Mutlaq Engineering has been an important player for over two decades,” said SMMA spokesperson Khalid Al-Saif. “Their difficulties reflect broader challenges faced by machinery makers, such as fluctuating demand and tight financing conditions.”

According to figures released by the administrators, a number of ongoing projects have been paused while the company assesses its ability to fulfill existing contracts. The administrators emphasized that their immediate focus is on stabilizing operations and safeguarding as many jobs as possible. “Our priority is to conduct a thorough review of Al-Mutlaq Engineering’s finances and identify viable paths forward, whether through restructuring or seeking new investment,” said lead administrator Noura Al-Farhan.

Analysts say the outcome for Al-Mutlaq Engineering remains uncertain. “The machinery sector in Saudi Arabia is under pressure, and firms with high debt levels are especially vulnerable,” said Faisal Al-Masoud, an industry analyst based in Riyadh. “If a turnaround cannot be achieved, there could be further consolidation within the sector.”

For now, production at Al-Mutlaq Engineering remains limited, and the company’s future hangs in the balance as the administration process proceeds.
